finding: research_policy.VOIPolicy is not a value-of-information computation. It is a hardcoded fixed preference order, ORDER=(REGULATORY_FILING, GOVERNMENT_DATA, INDEPENDENT_REPORTING, ANALYST_COVERAGE, COMPANY_OWNED), and its own docstring says it is 'here to be beaten'. Separately, evaluate_offline passes options=SOURCE_FAMILIES — all five families — for EVERY record, regardless of what was actually eligible for that decision.
implication: Because REGULATORY_FILING is first in ORDER and always present in the offered options, VOIPolicy is expected to be numerically identical to FixedPolicy(REGULATORY_FILING) on the current log. The reported 'VOI prefers filings' is therefore a property of a constant plus a fictitious choice set, not a miscalibrated heuristic. Falsifiable prediction to be measured under B-VOI-001.

evidence: 16 tests. Nine methods declared with question types, minimum samples, assumptions and failure modes; three implemented (persistence, drift, AR1). Walk-forward over 15 real macro series from the production ledger. Persistence best on 9, AR1 on 4, drift on 2. finding: On this corpus nothing reliably beats persistence for short-horizon macro LEVELS. That is the expected and useful answer: it sets the bar every later method must clear, and it is the reason the registry scores against persistence rather than against other methods.

evidence: Wrote the assumption tests, then ran them against the live macro series in reports/market/learning_ledger.jsonl.
finding: Two of the first implementations were wrong, and both were only visible against real data. (1) The stationarity screen used the lag-1 autocorrelation of the levels around their mean; the statistic the assumption is ABOUT is the fitted AR(1) coefficient, which is what the method actually estimates. On a monotone series the autocorrelation screen passed and the fitted coefficient is exactly 1.0. (2) Residual autocorrelation was computed from walk-forward forecast errors. An expanding-window fit chases the series, so those errors are negatively autocorrelated by construction and EVERY series failed the 'one lag carries the dependence' check, including a textbook AR(1). The assumption is about the in-sample residuals of one fit.
honest_reading: A check that fails on everything is as useless as one that passes on everything, and it is more convincing. Both defects produced plausible-looking output on the fixtures that were written to confirm them.
